wu: Warm-up: 'Guess the Item' — Teacher holds up flashcards of clothes one by one; students shout the English word; first to say correctly gets a point.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'Simon Says' with clothes commands like 'Simon says touch your shoes'.
Alternative 2: 'Clothes Bingo' — students draw 6 items from the list and cross them off as the teacher names them.
pres: Presentation: Show a story of a child getting dressed; use flashcards to introduce t-shirt, trousers, dress, shoes, hat, jacket; model 'She is wearing a red dress' and 'He has got a blue hat'; check understanding by asking 'What is he wearing?' and 'Has she got a hat?'
presAlt: Alternative 1: Use a realia bag with actual clothes items; students pull one out and say the word.
Alternative 2: Show a short video of someone dressing up; pause to name each item.
prac: Guided practice: 'Describe and Draw' — Teacher describes a person (e.g., 'She is wearing a yellow hat and green shoes'); students draw in pairs; walk around to help with spelling and pronunciation.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Matching Pairs' — students match clothing words to pictures on flashcards.
Alternative 2: 'Sentence Race' — teams race to write sentences like 'He is wearing a jacket' on the whiteboard.
ls: Listening slot: 'Listen and Draw' — Teacher describes a person (e.g., 'He has got a black jacket and brown shoes'); students draw on a worksheet; compare drawings in pairs to check comprehension.
re: Reactivation game: 'Fashion Show' — students walk down a 'catwalk' while saying what they are wearing (e.g., 'I am wearing a blue t-shirt and jeans'); others guess who it is.
prod: Production task: 'Guess Who?' — Students work in groups; one student describes a classmate (e.g., 'She is wearing a pink dress and a hat'); others guess who it is; present the best descriptions to the class.
rw: Reading and writing slot: 'Read and Match' — Students read short descriptions (e.g., 'He is wearing a blue jacket and trousers') and match them to photos; then write 3 sentences about their own outfit.
st: Story / song + goodbye: Sing 'Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes' with clothing variations; read a short story about a child choosing clothes for a festival; end with Goodbye Song + sticker chart + high-five line.
g: Teams race to dress a paper doll with flashcards.
Students close eyes; teacher removes one clothing item; they guess what's missing.
Students draw clothing items for others to guess.
Teacher says 'I spy something you wear on your feet'; students guess 'shoes'.
Students take turns describing what the teacher is wearing.
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write a 5-sentence description of a Moroccan festival outfit.
Support / weaker learners: Use word banks with pictures to help write sentences.
hw: Homework option 1: Read the clothes page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words.
Homework option 2: Draw a picture of yourself and write 3 sentences about what you are wearing.
Homework option 3: Interview a family member about their clothes and write 2 sentences.
tip: Use local context like the Green March or Independence Day to make descriptions relevant (e.g., 'He is wearing a green jacket for the Green March').
